name: Moche
capital: Moche (Huacas del Sol y de la Luna)
summary: A culture of Peru’s north coast famous for its realistic portrait pottery, gold work and huge adobe pyramids. The rich tomb of the Lord of Sipán was found in 1987.

location.value: River valleys of Peru’s north coast (modern La Libertad and Lambayeque).

terrain.value: Desert coast crossed by rivers from the Andes.

climate.value: Very dry, but hit by severe El Niño floods and droughts.

resources.value: Irrigated farmland, fish and seabird guano as fertiliser.

disasters.value: Severe El Niño events and drought around the 6th century may have weakened the Moche.

urbanisation.value: The southern capital was near present-day Moche, Trujillo, with the Huacas del Sol y de la Luna.

economicBase.value: Irrigation farming (maize, beans, squash, cotton) and fishing.

tradeRoutes.value: Exchange with highland peoples for wool and metals.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: No coinage; labour for building pyramids was organised in teams.

inequality.value: Lords buried with rich gold, silver and shell goods; commoners in simple graves.

governmentType.value: Culturally united but politically independent polities, not one empire.

keyRulers.value: No names survive; the Lord of Sipán (c. 250 CE) is known from his tomb.

succession.value: Unknown; probably hereditary elites, as rich burials suggest.

institutions.value: Large irrigation systems and organised labour.

stability.value: Regional polities rose and fell along the coast.

eliteConflict.value: Scenes of ritual combat and prisoner sacrifice appear on pottery.

armyAndTech.value: Warriors with clubs and shields shown on pottery.

majorWars.value: No specific wars are known; art shows warriors and captives.

territoryChange.value: Influence spread along about 250 miles of coast.

scienceEducation.value: No writing; possible symbolic marks on beans are debated.

communicationTransport.value: Travel on foot and with llamas along the coast; reed boats (caballitos de totora) for fishing.

languageWriting.value: Unknown, probably the Mochica language; no writing.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Moche culture (checked 6 Nov 2026); Bawden, The Moche (1996)

artsArchitecture.value: Rich iconography and monumental architecture: portrait vessels, murals and adobe pyramids.

socialStructure.value: Lords, priests, craftsmen, farmers and fishers.

sharedIdentity.value: A shared art style and religion across the valleys.

dailyLife.value: Adobe houses near huge pyramids (Huacas of the Sun and Moon); maize, beans, fish and guinea pig.

neighbours.value: The Nazca, Recuay and later Wari cultures.

ideasReligions.value: Influenced the later Sicán and Chimú cultures.

riseSignals.value: Emerged around 100 CE in the river valleys of northern Peru.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Moche culture (checked 6 Nov 2026); Bawden, The Moche (1996)

peakPeriod.value: About 300–600 CE, with the great Huacas built.

declineSignals.value: Climate disasters (El Niño floods and drought) and possibly unrest.

outcome.value: Ended about 800; succeeded by the Wari and Sicán cultures.

overallCertainty.value: Low to medium. With no writing, much is inferred from art. Second source: Wikidata gives 1–700 CE; Wikipedia gives c. 100–800 CE.

knownFor.label: Lord of Sipán tomb
knownFor.note: A richly furnished royal tomb found in 1987.

knownFor.label: Huaca del Sol
knownFor.note: One of the largest adobe structures in the Americas.
